segments.text: Good evening, welcome to the press conference. Please raise your hands, state your name
and organisation when asking questions. Rafa, you've got something to share with us.
Well, good evening everyone. Unfortunately, as you can imagine, if I am here because
I have to pull out from the tournament now. As everybody saw yesterday, I have been suffering
with the pain in the abdominal. I know something was not okay there, as yesterday I said.
And yeah, that's confirmed, I have a tear in the muscle, in the domino, so the communication
is too late because even like that I was thinking during the whole day about the
decision to make but I think it's yeah I think it's don't make sense to to go
and if I even if I try it a lot of time doing all my career to keep going
under very tough circumstances in that one I think it's obvious that if I
keep going the the injury gonna I'm gonna be worse and worse and and
And that's the thing that I can say now and I feel very sad to say that.
Have you made the decision primarily because you don't think you can be competitive in
a semi-final against Nick Kyrgios or because you're worried that by playing on you'll
make the injury that much worse?
I made my decision because I believe that I can't win two matches under these circumstances.
It's not only that I can't serve at the right speed, it's that I can't do the normal
movement to serve. After I said that, I imagined myself winning two matches and for respect
to myself in some way. I don't want to go out there, not be competitive enough to play
at the level that I need to play to achieve my goal and with a big chance to make the
things much worse. Being honest, a couple of weeks ago I saw my career very difficult
because of the foot injury, now that the things are better in that case and that's the most
dangerous things that can today stop my tennis career, thinking that the things are going
better in that way without a doubt. As I always said, for me the most important thing is
happiness more than any title, even if everybody knows how much effort I put to
to be here, but I can't risk that much and stay two or three months outside of the competition
because that's going to be a tough thing for me. If that happens, it happens, but
not because I was not doing the things the proper way. That's my decision and
I have to live with that and I can't say another thing that I am very sad and have been a very
tough one.
It's been a strange year with the Australian Open and the French Open where you have
physical limitations.
How frustrating is it for you to see your bid for the calendar slam end in this
year?
No, I never thought about the Calender Slam. I thought about my diary happiness and my
diary work and just play for the things that I really feel like. Honestly, Australia
was not an issue. I didn't have many problems during the tournament but I came
back from a long period of time of injury. Yeah, Roland Garros has been a very demanding
mentally, especially and physically one. But after that, things were going better.
As I said, after how tough Roland Garros was, just the fact that I was here shows
how important this tournament is for me and how much I wanted to play here.
I did all the things the best way possible to give myself a chance here and I am in
the semi-finals and playing very well the last couple of days, especially yesterday
before, at the beginning of the match, playing at a very, very high level, so even
that makes me feel a little bit worse because I felt that playing at the level
that I was playing, probably I will have a chance.

Rafael, you just told us that if you keep on playing it gets worse. You had the problems in the second set against Taylor Fritz already, your sister and your father said maybe you should quit. You kept on playing, was it the right position?
It was the right decision because I finished the match and I won the match, I did the things
that I felt in every single moment and I am not the kind of player and the kind of
person that when you make decisions I'm going to look back and say, okay, I should
not be doing that or I should do another thing.
Of course you learn from mistakes, I did during all my tennis career,
I tried to not repeat mistakes, but on the other hand,
I didn't want to pull out, to go out the court in the middle of a quarter-finals match.
and even if, as I said yesterday, the chance of retirement stays in my mind for a long
time after the first five, six games, I find a way to finish the match and something
that I am proud of and then you confirm that you have an injury and then you make the decision
thinking about your health and your future.
Hi Rafa, Eleanor Crooks, Press Association. Can you say when the injury happened and
do you know yet how long it will take you to recover?
Well, I had some issues in the dominoes in the week, but the things were more or less
able to control it. But yesterday was the worst day. I did tests to see how the things
evolves and it's obvious that yesterday, after the match, this very small thing that
I had years ago, sorry, days ago, increased to a bigger thing, you know, and that's
the thing. And I'm going to be around between three or four weeks, normal thing,
For this kind of injuries, so I hope that this will not
Make me I hope this
These three four weeks will allow me to do my normal calendar. That's that's my my
the calendar that I I have on mine, so I
Can keep playing not now, but in in one week
I'm going to be able to play from the baseline, not serving for a while of course, but playing
from the baseline is not going to be a big deal, so in some way that's a positive thing
that I want to keep being able to practice a bit from the baseline, and that helps
to try to make the calendar that I want to do.
Rafa, was there one point yesterday where it was really bad, where you aggravated
it, or was it just building up and then the pain got bad? Was there a certain point
where you reached or served hard or anything?
It's difficult to say. I had this feeling on the domino last week, but for some moments
were worse, some moments a little bit better. But yesterday, in the game that I was serving,
3-1 to 3-2 I think, was the moment that I started to feel the things were going worse.
and then serving, if I was not wrong, serving 4-3 the thing starts to be much worse.
Then I found a way more or less to even slow down, slowing down the speed and changing the movement on the serve.
I was able to find a way to probably not increase the injury that much, and be able to finish
the match, but yeah.
Then I am always the kind of person that thinks step by step.
Yesterday I wanted to, as I said, I wanted to finish the match.
I finished with a victory, but then I need to do all the things that I had to do.
And the test says that I have what I have.
There is always a choice, but in this particular case,
it's not like the foot that I know that the injury is there and the injury will not get worse.
in this particular case, it's obvious that if I keep going,
the injury is going to be increasing.
